summary: Fix to NFC food tags (#3411): when the amount screen switches a library food to a converted unit (oz on a gram food), the app first saves that unit as a serving of the food and points the tag at it, instead of producing a tag the server refuses; a serving edited to another unit asks for one of the food's servings. Part of the NFC tags feature (see #3316); no audit row.
evidence_note: SparkyFitnessMobile/src/screens/FoodEntryAddScreen.tsx (action-tag mode saves a converted unit as a serving before returning it)

summary: NFC tags can now log a food or a saved meal, not only water: setup offers 'Water or drink' and 'Food or meal' (the logging search and amount screen), 'Add NFC tag' rows on food and meal details, 'Log to' by time of day or a fixed meal type, and Undo removes exactly the logged entry. Scanning or creating a food inside a picker (water container, tag) now returns it instead of logging it. Server runs the food/meal actions. Same on iOS and Android; not on the web. Extends the NFC tags new feature from #3316 (one entry).

new_feature.name: NFC tags: log water, a food or a saved meal with a tap (same entry as #3316)
new_feature.description: Set up an NFC sticker from Settings > NFC tags, a water container, a food or a saved meal; one tap with the phone (app closed or open) logs the drink, food or meal saved with the tag, with Undo, optional 'Ask before logging', double-tap protection and meal type by time of day or fixed. The tag holds only a https://tag.sparkyfitness.com/t/<code> link; the action is stored on the user's server. iPhone (XS or later) shows a banner to tap; Android 15 and older opens the app directly, Android 16 may show a notification first; Android shows its own waiting card and asks to turn NFC on, iPhone uses the system sheet. Not on the web. Translated into de, fr, pl, pt-BR only.
